semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {اقرأ}: The majority read with sukūn on the hamza, as an imperative from القراءة (reading). ʿĀṣim, in the transmission of al-Aʿshā, read it with a fatḥa-voweled rāʾ [and no hamza], as though he changed the hamza into an alif, as in their saying قرا يَقْرا, like سعَى يَسْعى; then, when he formed the imperative from it, he omitted the alif in the same way as it is omitted from اسْعَ. This is like the saying of Zuhayr:
4603 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وإلاَّ يُبْدَ بالظُّلْمِ يُظْلَمِ
(…and if he does not begin with wrongdoing, he will be wronged.)
Its exposition has already been given.
His saying: {باسم رَبِّكَ}: Several views are possible on it. The first: the bāʾ is circumstantial (for the ḥāl), i.e. read, beginning with the name of your Lord: say "In the name of Allah", then read. Al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: the bāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), the implied form being: read the name of your Lord, as in his saying:
4604 -. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... سُوْدُ المَحاجِرِ لا يَقْرَأْنَ بالسُّوَرِ
(…dark around the eyes, they do not recite the sūras.)
It was also said: the [word] «اسم» is redundant (ṣila), i.e. remember your Lord. Abū ʿUbayda said both of these. The third: the bāʾ is for seeking aid (istiʿāna) and the object is omitted, its implied form being: read what is revealed to you, seeking aid by the name of your Lord. The fourth: it is in the sense of «على», i.e. read upon the name of your Lord, as in His saying: {وَقَالَ اركبوا فِيهَا بِسْمِ الله} [Hūd: 41]; al-Akhfash said this. It has already been discussed at the beginning of this work how this verb was placed before the preposition [here] while it was supplied as coming after it in «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم», together with people's explanations of that, so that suffices instead of repeating it.
His saying: {الذي خَلَقَ خَلَقَ الإنسان}: The second «خَلَقَ» may be an explanation of the first «خَلَقَ», meaning that He left it vague at first and then explained it secondly by the creation of man, to magnify the creation of man. It is also possible that He omitted the object from the first, its implied form being: He created everything, because it is unrestricted and so covers every created thing.

semin-durr:2-2.t: And His saying: {خَلَقَ الإنسان}: a singling out of him for mention among all that creation covers, because the revelation is [sent down] to him. It may also be a verbal emphasis (tawkīd lafẓī), in which case He would have emphasised the ṣila (relative clause) alone, as in your saying: «الذي قام قام زيدٌ» (the one who stood — Zayd stood). What is meant by الإنسان is the genus; that is why He said: {مِنْ عَلَقٍ}, the plural of عَلَقة (clinging clot), because each one is created from a clot, as in the other verse.

semin-durr:4-4.t: And His saying: {الذى عَلَّمَ بالقلم عَلَّمَ الإنسان مَا لَمْ يَعْلَمْ}: close to His saying: «خَلَق، خلَق الإِنسانَ», so you may apply here again what has preceded.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {أَن رَّآهُ}: «أنْ» [with its clause] is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. because he sees himself as self-sufficient. The verb here passes over to its two attached pronouns [subject and object referring to the same person], because this is among the special features of this class [of verbs]. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «The meaning of seeing is knowing; had it been in the sense of seeing with the eyes, combining the two pronouns would be prohibited with its verb; and "استغنى" is the second object.» I say: there is disagreement on the question. A group held that «رأى» of eyesight is given the ruling of «رأى» of knowledge, and they counted among this the saying of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her: «لقد رَأَيْتُنا مع رسولِ الله ﷺ وما لنا طعامٌ إلاَّ الأسْوَدان» (we saw ourselves with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ having no food but the two black things), and he quoted:
4605 - ولقد أَراني للرِّماح دَرِيْئَةً ... مِنْ عَنْ يمين تارةً وأمامي
(I have seen myself as a target for the spears, at times from my right and [at times] before me.)
Its verification has already been given. Qunbul — with disagreement [among the transmitters] from him — read «رَأَه» without an alif after the hamza; it is shortened from «رآه» in the reading of the majority. There is no doubt that omission in such a case has occurred rarely, as in their saying: «اصابَ الناسَ جَهْدٌ، ولو تَرَ أهلَ مكةَ» (hardship befell the people — if only you saw the people of Mecca), with omission of the final radical of «ترى», and the saying of the other:
4606 - وَصَّانِيَ العَجَّاجُ فيما وَصَّني ...
(Al-ʿAjjāj enjoined me in what he enjoined me.)
meaning: وصَّاني. When Ibn Mujāhid related this reading from Qunbul — and he said: «I read it so before him» — he attributed it to error. [Translator's note: the text reads «الغلظ» (coarseness), evidently for «الغلط» (error); translated accordingly.] That is not proper, because when a reading is established and has a valid rationale, even if another is better known than it, one should not venture to declare it erroneous.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {أَرَأَيْتَ الذي}: The discussion of this word has already been given to you in full. Al-Zamakhsharī has a discussion here which I saw fit to mention because of a particularity relating to it. He said: «If you say: what is the object of "أَرَأَيْت"? I say: "الذي يَنْهى" together with the conditional clause; they are in the position of the two objects. If you say: then where is the apodosis (jawāb) of the condition? I say: it is omitted, its implied form being: if he is upon guidance or commands piety, does he not know that Allah sees? It was omitted only because its mention in the apodosis of the second condition indicates it. If you say: how is it valid for "ألم يعلَمْ" to be the apodosis of the condition? I say: just as it is valid in your saying: "إنْ أَكْرَمْتُك أتكرِمُني" (if I honour you, will you honour me?) and "إن أَحْسَنَ إليك زيدٌ هل تُحْسِنُ إليه؟" (if Zayd does good to you, will you do good to him?). If you say: then what is the second "أَرَأَيْتَ" and its coming between the two objects of "أَرَأَيْتَ"? I say: it is redundant (zāʾida), repeated for emphasis.» I say: since he has entered into discussing this verse, let us go along with him.
Know that «أرَأَيْتَ» — as you have learned — has as its second object only an interrogative clause, as in His saying: {أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُهُ} [Yūnus: 50] to its end, and similar cases are many. Here «أرَأَيْتَ» occurs three times, and after the third of them an interrogative clause is stated explicitly, so it is in the position of its second object; its first object is omitted, and it is a pronoun referring to «الذي ينهى», which occurs as the first object of the first «أَرَأَيْتَ». The object of the first «أَرَأيْتَ» that is the second [object] is omitted, and it is an interrogative clause like the clause occurring after the third «أَرَأَيْتَ». As for the second «أرأَيْتَ», no object is mentioned for it, neither first nor second: the first was omitted because the object of the first «أَرَأَيْتَ» indicates it, and the second was omitted because the object of the third «أَرَأَيْتَ» indicates it. So the second [object] was omitted from the first, the first from the third, and both from the second. The demand of each «أَرَأَيْتَ» for the nominal clause is not by way of contention (tanāzuʿ), because that calls for an implied pronoun, and clauses are not implied as pronouns — only single words are; rather, it is of the class of omission because of an indication. [Translator's note: «الجملة الاسمية» (the nominal clause) is as written; the preceding argument concerns the interrogative clause (الاستفهامية).] As for the discussion of the condition together with this «أَرَأَيْتَ», you have learned it from what is in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām, so we will not lengthen the discussion by repeating it. [Translator's note: the text reads «في نُطيل», evidently for «فلا نُطيل».] Al-Zamakhsharī's allowing the apodosis of the condition to be an interrogative by itself is not permissible; rather, they stipulated that the fāʾ must be mentioned in such a case, and if anything [to the contrary] occurs, it is poetic licence (ḍarūra).

semin-durr:15-15.t:
His saying: {لَنَسْفَعاً}: In pause, this nūn is pronounced as an alif, likening it to tanwīn; and likewise it is omitted after a ḍamma and a kasra in pause. Here it is written as an alif, following the pause. It is related from Abū ʿAmr: «لَنَسْفَعَنَّ» with the heavy nūn. السَّفْع is seizing and grasping a thing firmly and dragging it. ʿAmr ibn Maʿdīkarib said:
4607 - قومٌ إذا سَمِعُوا الصَّريخَ رَأَيْتَهُمْ ... ما بين مُلْجمِ مُهْرِه أو سافعِ
(A people who, when they hear the cry for help, you see them either bridling their colts or seizing [their forelocks].)
It was also said: it is "taking" in the dialect of Quraysh. Al-Rāghib said: «السَّفْع is seizing the horse by its سُفْعة, i.e. the blackness of its forelock. With regard to blackness the hearthstones were called "سُفْع", and "به سُفْعَةُ غَضَبٍ" (he has a flush of anger), with regard to the smoky colour that comes over the face of one whose anger has become intense; and the falcon was called "أسْفَعُ" because of the glints of black in it; and a woman سَفْعاءُ اللونِ (dark-complexioned).» End of quotation. In the ḥadīth: «فقامَتِ امرأةٌ سَفْعاءُ الخَدَّيْن» (a woman with dark cheeks stood up).

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {نَاصِيَةٍ كَاذِبَةٍ}: a badal (substitute) from «الناصية», the substitution of an indefinite for a definite. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «Its substitution for the definite, while it is indefinite, was permissible because it is described [by an adjective], so it conveys a meaning on its own.» I say: this is the doctrine of the Kufans; they do not permit substituting an indefinite for something else except on condition that it is described or that it has the same wording as the first; the doctrine of the Basrans stipulates nothing, and they quoted:
4608 - فلا وأبيك خيرٍ منك إنِّي ... لَيُوْذِيْنيْ التَّحَمْحُمُ والصَّهيلُ
(No, by your father — one better than you — the neighing and whinnying do trouble me.)
Abū Ḥaywa, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «ناصيةً كاذبةً خاطئةً» in the accusative, by way of reviling (shatm). Al-Kisāʾī, in one transmission, read it in the nominative, on the implied [mubtadaʾ]: "it is a forelock". Lying and sinning were attributed to it figuratively. The alif and lām in «الناصية» — it was said: they compensate for the annexation, i.e. "by his forelock"; it was also said: the pronoun is omitted, i.e. "the forelock of him".

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {فَلْيَدْعُ نَادِيَهُ}: This is either by omission of a muḍāf, i.e. the people of his assembly, or by figurative usage in calling the assembly, because it contains the people, as in His saying: {وَسْئَلِ القرية} [Yūsuf: 82]. النادي and النَّدِيّ are the gathering place taken for conversation. Zuhayr said:
4609 - وفيهم مَقاماتٌ حِسانٌ وجوهُهُمْ ... وأَنْدِيَةٌ يَنْتابُها القولُ والفِعْلُ
(Among them are gatherings of fair-faced men, and assemblies frequented by [wise] word and deed.)
A Bedouin woman said: «He is the chief of his assembly and the support of those seeking his favour.»

semin-durr:18-18.t:
His saying: {الزبانية}: Al-Zamakhsharī said: «الزَّبانية in the speech of the Arabs are the police (shuraṭ); the singular is زِبْنِيَة like عِفْرِية, from الزَّبْن, which is pushing. It was also said: زِبْنيّ, as though it were related to الزَّبْن and then altered for the relation (nisba), as in their saying إمْسيّ; its origin is زَبانيّ, and then زبانِيَة was said by way of compensation.» ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar and al-Akhfash said: «Its singular is زابِن.» It was also said: it has no singular from its own wording, like عَباديد and شماطيط. The upshot is that the root denotes pushing. He said:
4610 - مطاعيمُ في القُصْوى مطاعينُ في الوغَى ... زبانيَةٌ غُلْبٌ عِظامٌ حُلُومُها
(Feeders [of guests] in the hardest times, thrusters [with spears] in battle, mighty repellers, thick-necked, great in their forbearance.)
Another said:
4611 - ومُسْتَعْجِبٍ مِمَّا يرى مِنْ أناتِنا ... ولو زَبَنَتْه الحَرْبُ لم يَتَرَمْرَمِ
(Many a one marvels at the patience he sees in us; yet had war pushed him, he would not have uttered a word.)
ʿUtba said: «War has pushed us and we have pushed it.» From it is الزُّبون (customer), because he is pushed from one seller to another. The majority read «سَنَدْعُ» with the nūn of majesty; it is not written with a wāw, and its parallel has already been given, as in «يَدْعُ الداعِ». Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «سيدعى الزبانيةُ» as passive, with «الزَّبانية» in the nominative because it stands in place of the fāʿil (agent).
